exercise1.prompt: The shape of every group-by, named once so the rest makes sense.

hiddenCases.name: the mean is of the group, not the whole table
groupby does the splitting
hiddenCases.describe: a groupby rather than a hand-written loop

exercise1.hint: groupby the subject, take the score column, ask for the mean, round it, and to_dict() at the end gives plain keys and values.

questions.prompt: Put the three steps of a group-by in order.
items: Combine the answers into one result
Split the rows by a key
Apply a summary to each group
questions.explain: Split, apply, combine. Naming the three makes the shape of every group-by recognisable, however complicated the summary is.

questions.prompt: What becomes the index of a group-by result?
questions.explain: One row per group, labelled by the group key, which is why the result reads as a lookup table.

questions.prompt: Why is a group-by better than looping over the distinct values yourself?
choices: It does the split once, and it is easy to get the loop subtly wrong
questions.explain: The common bug in the hand-written version is summarising the whole table inside the loop instead of the group -- which is exactly the wrong answer the exercise checks for.
